newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cane body supports sugar tariff end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cane body supports sugar tariff end.

text.p: Queensland sugarcane growers have welcomed the Federal government's "belated" decision to abolish tariffs on sugar imports from July 1, Harry Bonanno, chairman of grower organisation CANEGROWERS, said on Tuesday.
Bonanno called on the government to ensure that other industries "face up to economic reality in the same way that sugar has done".

Bonanno was commenting on a statement by Australian Prime Minister John Howard earlier on Tuesday that the A$55 a tonne tariff on imported raw and refined sugar would be abolished, as recommended by the Sugar Industry Review report last December.
"The government must put the blowtorch of national competition policy to the belly of other industries which continue to enjoy protection," Bonanno said in a statement.
Removal of the sugar import tariff would adversely affect the finances of individual sugarcane growers, he said.

But it was accepted that the package was the only way the sugar industry could satisfy national competition policy and retain single desk export selling, collective negotiation between growers and mill-owners and industry overview of production and marketing, he said.
